brief.headline: Cristian fell on Oct 3, 2026 and now needs moderate help with bathing. He has also lost about 8% of his weight since Sep 5, and since about Oct 23 he has been more confused in the evenings.

items.statement: On Nov 6, 2026 his niece Kevin reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. Cristian was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The RN planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. The evidence provided does not show results or a visit.
items.verifier_note: All details match the Nov 6 note. The statement that no results or visit appear in the evidence is accurate, because the encounters record is empty.

items.statement: Cristian fell at home on Oct 3, 2026 getting out of bed and was found on the floor by Kevin. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness, and no injury was noted. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: The Oct 3 note matches every detail: the fall getting out of bed, Kevin finding him, no head strike or LOC, no injury, high fall risk, and the PT referral.

items.statement: PT evaluation on Oct 10, 2026 found a slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see him twice weekly. The evidence does not show whether the equipment or evaluation are in place.
items.verifier_note: The Oct 10 PT note matches every detail: the gait findings, TUG of 19 seconds, the three recommendations, and twice-weekly visits. The note says nothing about whether equipment or the evaluation are in place.

items.statement: Weight fell from 110.8 kg on Sep 5 to 102.3 kg on Nov 24, 2026, a loss of 8.5 kg (7.7%). It dropped steadily across readings on Oct 1 (107.8 kg) and Oct 28 (104.8 kg). He reports poor appetite, skips breakfast and eats about 50% of day center lunches. The dietitian planned an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record supports the weights, the 8.5 kg loss and the 7.7%. The dietitian note supports the appetite, breakfast and lunch details and the plan. The note rounds the loss to 8%, which is consistent with 7.7%.

items.statement: On Sep 29, 2026 OT found he now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, and he was independent at the last review. On Sep 21 he needed hands-on help out of the tub and said he was skipping showers for fear of slipping. OT recommended a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 29 OT note and Sep 21 aide note support every detail, including the earlier independence, the tub help, the skipped showers, and the three recommendations.

items.statement: There is no influenza vaccine on record for the season that began Aug 1, 2026. His last flu vaccine was Dec 22, 2025.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season (season start Aug 1, 2026) and a last flu vaccine on 2025-12-22.

questions_for_team: Have the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit for the evening confusion been done, and what did they show?
Could the fall, the weight loss and the new confusion be related, and who is coordinating the workup?
Are the walker, tub transfer bench, handheld shower, grab bars and added bathing hours in place? Is the stove a safety concern at home?
Is the dietitian's plan (supplements, weekly weights, dental check) under way, and is further weight loss being tracked?
Should the flu vaccine be offered now?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, and hospital admissions in that window, plus any discharge summaries not yet reconciled.
Falls and near-falls review: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether any occurred while on the new osteoporosis-related treatment; check fall-risk screen status and any post-fall follow-up.
Fracture screen: any new fractures or fracture-related visits given the osteoporosis diagnosis (onset 2025-12-22); check bone density follow-up and calcium/vitamin D documentation.

Alendronic acid (started 2025-12-22): confirm adherence, administration instructions being followed (upright, empty stomach, water), and any GI symptoms, dysphagia, heartburn, or missed doses; confirm dental and renal status are documented.

Cardiac medication review: metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, simvastatin, and nitroglycerin spray; check for any new starts, stops, dose changes, or refill gaps; check for bleeding events given clopidogrel use and anemia history.
Chest pain or angina episodes in the window, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, and any cardiology visits or ECG results related to ischemic heart disease.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend in the window, including orthostatic readings given beta-blocker use and fall risk; flag any readings outside the team's set thresholds.
Weight and BMI trend (obesity, BMI 30+): compare current weight to last review, note any unintended weight loss or gain, and check nutrition and dietary counseling status.
Glycemic check for prediabetes: review most recent HbA1c or fasting glucose, date of last test, and whether repeat testing or lifestyle follow-up is due.
Anemia follow-up: review most recent hemoglobin/CBC, iron studies if any, and any bleeding signs (given clopidogrel) or fatigue reported in the window.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: compare current ADL and IADL status to the prior review, including mobility, transfers, and stair use; note any new assistive device needs.
Cognition, mood, and engagement: check any cognitive screen scores, depression screen (PHQ) results, social engagement and program attendance, and any reported changes in sleep or appetite.
Caregiver and home situation: confirm current caregiver availability, any caregiver strain reported, living situation changes, and home safety concerns (age 91, fall risk).

Care-plan items due: list goals, reassessments, and any overdue items (e.g., annual labs, bone density, vaccinations, advance directive or code status review, medication reconciliation) with due dates in or before the review date of 2026-11-30.
Allergy record: allergy list is empty; verify with participant and family and flag for the team to confirm it is accurate.
